edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Frailty leaves less physiologic margin for surgery, so stress responses, immobility, and wound-healing demands more easily tip into complications.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2022 Li cohort in BMC Anesthesiol, which ties frailty index to postoperative complications in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.

evidence.notes: The composite risk index based on frailty predicts postoperative complications in older patients recovering from elective digestive tract surgery: a retrospective cohort study.
